## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A seven-*juan* Northern-Sòng treatise on the Lotus Sūtra collaboratively authored by two of the most significant figures of late-Northern-Sòng Buddhist intellectual culture: the Línjì 臨濟 Chán master and Buddhist literary historian [慧洪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%B4%AA) Juéfàn Huìhóng (1071–1128) and the Hànlín statesman and lay Buddhist [張商英](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%95%86%E8%8B%B1) Wújìn jūshì Zhāng Shāngyīng (1043–1121). The work belongs to the late-Northern-Sòng *Chánjiào héyī* 禪教合一 ("Chán and doctrinal teaching are one") synthetic project — the institutional and intellectual movement that sought to integrate Chán practice with the doctrinal apparatus of the *jiàoxià* 教下 (doctrinal-school) traditions, particularly Tiāntái and Huāyán. Preserved as X30n0603 in the *Xùzàngjīng*.

**Abstract**

The *Hélùn* — "combined treatise" — is a distinctive late-Northern-Sòng productive form in which a Chán master and a lay scholar collaborated to produce a unified treatise that integrates Chán meditative-experiential reading of a Mahāyāna scripture with literary-doctrinal-political exposition. Huìhóng provided the Chán-experiential and doctrinal core of the work (the *zào* 造, "construction"), while Zhāng Shāngyīng provided the literary-political framing and editorial finalisation (the *zhuàn* 撰, "composition"). The two-name authorship is significant: it represents the joint Chán-and-lay-scholar productive form characteristic of late-Northern-Sòng literati Buddhism, in which monastic and lay Buddhist intellectuals collaborated as institutional equals in the production of major scholarly works.

The work's content reflects the *Chánjiào héyī* synthesis: it reads the Lotus Sūtra through both the Chán *yīxīn* 一心 (one-mind) framework and the broader Mahāyāna *jiàoxià* doctrinal apparatus, drawing on Tiāntái, Huāyán, and Yogācāra interpretive traditions for supplementary doctrinal discussion. The combination is characteristic of Huìhóng's broader literary-doctrinal project (visible also in his *Línjì zōngzhǐ* 臨濟宗旨 ([KR6q0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0126)) and the *Zhìmén bǎoxùn* 智門寶訓 ([智門寶訓](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Titles/%E6%99%BA%E9%96%80%E5%AF%B6%E8%A8%93))) and of Zhāng Shāngyīng's Buddhist literary corpus (visible also in his *Hùfǎ lùn* 護法論 ([KR6r0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0147), T2114)).

The dating must postdate the formation of the Huìhóng-Zhāng Shāngyīng collaboration (early 12th century) and predate Huìhóng's death (1128). A defensible bracket of c. 1100–1128 covers the productive period.

The two collaborators were principal figures of late-Northern-Sòng Buddhist intellectual culture: Huìhóng was the most important Northern-Sòng Chán literary historian (author of the *Sēngbǎo zhuàn* 僧寶傳 ([KR6q0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0040)), the *Línjì zōngzhǐ* ([KR6q0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0126)), and the *Lěngzhāi yèhuà* 冷齋夜話 ([KR3j0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0100))); Zhāng Shāngyīng was the chief minister (*zǎixiàng* 宰相) under [徽宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%BD%E5%AE%97) Huīzōng and the most influential lay Buddhist of the late Northern Sòng (author of the *Hùfǎ lùn* ([KR6r0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0147)) defending Buddhism against Daoist polemic, the *Sū Cháo sòng* 蘇朝頌 ([蘇朝頌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Titles/%E8%98%87%E6%9C%9D%E9%A0%8C)) commemorating [蘇軾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BB%BE) Sū Shì, and various Buddhist memorials).
